claims_extracted: The New York Fed source reports that benchmark Treasury trading activity concentrates on the last trading day of the month.
The source attributes the pattern plausibly to turn-of-month portfolio rebalancing by passive investment funds.
The source reports the end-of-month activity was associated with lower price impact and improved liquidity in Treasury markets.
The repo implementation maps the mechanism to an EURUSD M15 calendar-flow screen without claiming MT5 data equivalence or profitability.
limitations: The source is Treasury-market evidence, not direct EURUSD or FTMO broker evidence.
End-of-month liquidity improvement in Treasuries may not transfer to retail FX CFD bars.
The screen uses OHLCV and calendar timing only; it does not observe actual institutional rebalancing orders.
The current CSV is research data and does not prove FTMO terminal history equivalence.
disconfirming_relevance: EURUSD spot/CFD market structure differs from benchmark Treasury interdealer markets.
FX month-end flows can be absorbed before M15 bars show a stable signal.
Calendar effects can be unstable and prone to data-snooping if not pre-registered.
